premises: Nanohierarchical architecture with nano-coupled grains and nanoprecipitates yields ultralow wear in a complex concentrated alloy from RT to 800 °C.
The cooperative heterostructure activates a dense nanocrystalline glaze layer at 800 °C to minimize adhesive and oxidative wear.
The same heterostructure accommodates gradient frictional stress at room temperature via multiple deformation pathways.
A controlled thermomechanical treatment (cold rolling + gradient annealing) can produce a similar gradient nanohierarchical microstructure in CoCrFeNi.
The resulting microstructure will form an adaptive glaze layer in situ during sliding, reducing friction and wear across the full temperature range.
